# regen-comments

Rebuild docstrings and inline comments for Python file(s) **from the code's behavior**, in a chosen voice. Every model layer that reads or judges the code runs in a **clean room** (`claude -p` from `/tmp`) so a project `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` or the file's own stale comments cannot leak into the output. You (the in-session orchestrator) do only mechanical work and the human gates; you never judge code yourself.

## Inputs and modes
- **target** (natural language, a path, a file, or a method — the user never types `--lib`): the user says what they want in their own words, a path, or a flag, and the orchestrator resolves it to a target + genre + scope (the table in [Targeting, genre, and scope](#targeting-genre-and-scope) maps every form) and **confirms at the gate before running**.
- **genre** (`code` | `test` | `functional_test` | `example`): selects the triage aim AND the writer shape. Detected from the path (`tests/`→test, `functional_tests/`→functional_test, `examples/`→example, else code) OR from the words/flags the user uses — "unit tests" / `--tests`, "functional tests" / `--functional-tests`, "examples" / `--examples`. A bare library defaults to its **source** (`code`). `--kind <genre>` overrides.
- **scope**: **method** (one symbol), **file**, **folder**, or **whole library** (`--all`). A flagged method → only that method; a flagged file → only that file. `--all` runs all four lanes (source + tests + functional_tests + examples) over a library — **costly and slow; confirm the cost first** (invariant 7).
- **library-aware mode** (folder / library / `--all` scope, Runbook step 1b): a one-time library triage builds `LIBRARY_FACTS.md`, then the procedure loops per file with that cross-file ledger rode into every room. The orchestrator builds it and passes `--lib` to the phases **automatically** — `--lib` is internal plumbing, not a user flag.
- **`--voice <key>`** (optional): pick a voice from the shared registry (`../_shared/voices/voices.json`). The default is **voiceless** (`plain`) — it reads cleanest and is the right choice for most runs; a named voice is optional flavor. A voiced run also injects the voice's real-text excerpt from `voice_samples/<key>.md` into the writer prompt as a register sample (excerpt prose only — attribution never reaches the prompt; voices without a sample file run without one). If `--voice` is omitted, print [the voice pick menu](#the-voice-pick-menu-when-no---voice) and wait for the user's pick. **A run takes 1 voice (or none); pass up to 3 — `--voice a,b,c`, or 2–3 menu picks — to generate each and compare them side by side, then apply one.**
- **`--without-comment-triage`** (default: comment-triage **ON**): by default the file's *existing* comments are mined for genuinely non-derivable facts. Pass this flag to skip that lens and work purely from code. Writers stay clean-room either way; comment knowledge enters only through the (filtered) ledger. Copyright/license/author **header preservation is mechanical and always-on**, independent of this flag.
- **`--tight`** (optional, `code` genre): the minimal mode — each symbol gets a docstring of **one sentence (at most two when the contract earns it) covering behavior + caller contract only, with nothing after it**: no body paragraphs, no Args/Returns/Raises sections. **Traps and line mechanics ride as `#` comments at their lines**, in the voice; no clause-stuffing; a symbol with no ledger fact and a name that says everything gets **no docstring at all**. A fact that will not fit as a clean sentence is **dropped rather than compressed** (tight trades completeness for brevity — default mode is the complete one). The selector rejects bodies, sections, 3+-sentence docstrings, and crammed facts. Implements the workspace's strict-no-body docstring rule as a run mode. (`test`/`functional_test` are already summary-only by genre; `example` ignores the flag — dense annotation is its job.) Threads through `regen_phase2.py --tight`, `regen_batch.py phase2 ... --tight`, and `regen_phase2_multi.py ... --tight`; phase 2 records the run shape in `$RUN/phase2.json` (voice + genre + tight/less) so the refine loop regenerates in the SAME shape — `regen_symbol.py` and `tighten_symbol.py` read it (without it, a mid-refine regen fell back to the default code shape).
- **`--less`** (optional, `code` genre): the middle mode — a **single sentence summary line**, then (after a blank line) a **tiny body of a sentence or two in a few spots where a fact earns it**, then **short Args/Returns/Raises sections** where they apply, each entry a single short sentence, never padded into prose. Same behavior-only docstring rule and drop-rather-than-compress trade as `--tight`; traps and mechanics stay in `#` comments. Sits between `--tight` (no bodies, no sections) and default (fuller bodies). Mutually exclusive with `--tight`. Threads through the same drivers (`--less`) and `phase2.json`.
- **`--create-voice`** (mode): add a voice to `voices.json` — see [Creating a voice](#creating-a-voice---create-voice). Voices are data; never author a per-voice agent file.
- **Model:** every clean-room layer runs on **opus** (correctness-first; the lenses do the hard cross-method discovery and the validator gates correctness).
- **Passes:** **4** writer passes, then a best-of-4 selection (the most readable whole pass wins).

### The voice pick menu (when no `--voice`)
The FIRST human gate — it precedes everything else. Print an **in-session numbered text menu** built from the shared registry (`../_shared/voices/voices.json`), NOT an `AskUserQuestion`: the registry holds more voices than the tool's 4-option cap allows, and cramming it into four options is what made the old menu error out mid-run. List **every** voice in registry order with `plain` first, marked **(default, voiceless — reads cleanest)**; for each, show its one-line persona from `voices` plus the **first sentence** of its cached `previews` sample as a taste (offer to print any voice's full sample on request). **Render it spaced so the options don't run together — a blank line between each numbered entry, the persona on the number's line, the preview taste on its own indented line beneath, and a blank line before the closing prompt:**

```
  1. plain   (default, voiceless — reads cleanest)
       e.g. <first sentence of plain's cached preview>

  2. cantrill   — a direct, opinionated systems-engineering voice that names what is fragile and why
       e.g. <first sentence of cantrill's cached preview>

  … (one spaced block per voice) …

type a number or key to pick — or up to 3 (e.g. `2 5 8`) to compare — most runs take 1 (plain).
```

Then stop and wait for the user's reply. Map the reply to the voice key(s) and proceed: **1 pick → the normal run; 2–3 picks → a comparison run** (Runbook step 5b — each voice generated in its own room, the report compares them side by side, the human applies one). `--voice <key>` — or `--voice a,b,c` (up to 3, comma-separated) — skips this menu entirely.

### Targeting, genre, and scope
The orchestrator resolves what the user said — prose, a path, or a flag — into a **target**, a **genre**, and a **scope**, then confirms all three at the gate (with the voice pick) before any phase runs. The user never types `--lib`: name the library, file, method, or folder and the orchestrator finds it.

| User says | Target | Genre | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| a path to a `.py` file | that file | by path | file |
| "`<lib>` library" / a library name or source dir | that library's source | `code` | folder (source) |
| "`<lib>` `<file>.py`" / a file name | that file | by path | file |
| "the `<method>` in `<file>`" / a flagged method | that one symbol | by file path | **method only** |
| "`<lib>` unit tests" / `--tests` | that library's `tests/` | `test` | folder |
| "`<lib>` functional tests" / `--functional-tests` | that library's `functional_tests/` | `functional_test` | folder |
| "`<lib>` examples" / `--examples` | that library's `examples/` | `example` | folder |
| a `tests/` / `functional_tests/` / `examples/` folder path | files in it | by folder | folder |
| `--all` (with a library) | source + all three lanes | per-lane | **whole library** |

- **Verify before a folder lane.** Before a `tests/` / `functional_tests/` / `examples/` run, `ls` the folder; if it does not exist, say so and stop — never fabricate a lane.
- **A bare library = its source** (`code`); add a word or flag to pick a different lane.
- **`--all` is costly** (four lanes × every file). Push back (invariant 7): state the rough scale and confirm before running.
- **Voice applies to every genre** — always pick a voice at the gate (or `--voice <key>`). The genre sets the *shape*; the voice tunes the *register* on top, default `plain`.

What each genre changes (the triage aim in phase 1 and the writer shape in phase 2):
- **`code`** (default): trap triage (3 lenses + validator loop) → docstrings stating **behavior + the caller's contract**, line-mechanics as inline comments, Args/Returns.
- **`test`**: a per-test **claim** ledger → each test docstring names in one sentence the behavior the *subject under test* verifies (subject acting); **no Args/Returns/Raises, no body**; an above-line comment only on a non-obvious setup value. Module docstring = one sentence (+ a cross-runtime line if the file declares one).
- **`functional_test`**: same as `test`, at **end-to-end / scenario altitude** — the behavior exercised against the real runtime, device, or socket.
- **`example`**: a near-line **annotation plan** → a verb-led module summary + a use-case / how-to-run body, then a short comment on **nearly every meaningful line** giving *what it does* and *why it is in the example* (effect + teaching intent, never bare syntax). Every import preserved; stays a flat script; no invented output.

Scope mechanics:
- **method** — run phase 1 + phase 2 on the file for context (the writer needs the surrounding code + the ledger), then `regen_method.py <file> $RUN <voice> <symbol>` splices ONLY that symbol's new docstring/comments onto the ORIGINAL file (every other symbol keeps its existing comments) and verifies code identity; present/apply only that symbol.
- **file** — the single-file procedure (Runbook 0–8).
- **folder** — library-batch the files under one genre (`regen_batch.py phase1 <conc> --kind <genre> <files>`), pickers per room, then batch phase 2.
- **library / `--all`** — per lane: resolve the lane's folder, run its batch with that `--kind`, read its manifest before the next lane overwrites it. Confirm cost first.

## Invariants (do not violate)
1. **Clean room for every code-reading/judging layer.** Lenses, ledger-writer, writers, selector, verifier all run as `claude -p` launched **from a `/tmp` room**, never the in-session Workflow tool. Flags: `--allowedTools Read Write [Workflow Task] --permission-mode acceptEdits --model opus`. Never pass `--add-dir` pointing at the project (it would re-add a `CLAUDE.md` dir). Never use `bypassPermissions`.
2. **You are the only interactive layer.** Orchestrator does: mechanical strip, launching the `claude -p` phases, the human picker, mechanical reattach, presentation. Headless `claude -p` cannot ask the user anything — so the human gate lives only here, *between* phases. Every `AskUserQuestion` gate must honor the tool's hard limits or it errors out mid-run: **2–4 options** (never 1, never 5+), `header` **≤ 12 chars**, and **no `preview` on a multi-select**. When a choice would exceed 4 options (the voice registry, a long questionable-facts list), use an in-session numbered text menu and have the user type the number(s); when it would fall to 1 (a lone questionable fact), use a 2-option Keep / Drop instead. The interactive pages add a **second human-gate channel**: the decision page (`picker.html`, on the shared picker at `../_shared/picker/`) and `compare.html` carry checkable picks + notes + a **Copy selection** button whose blob the human pastes back into the session — and, when served (`../_shared/picker/serve_picker.py` for the decision page, `serve_report.py` for `compare.html`), a **Submit to session** button that lands the same blob at the dir's `selection.txt` and reaches the session as a Monitor event (transport only; the page never applies anything). Either way the orchestrator parses it with `apply_selection.py` and treats it exactly like answers typed in chat — the invariant-7 push-backs still happen in-session after parsing, never in the page.
3. **Writers never see the original comments.** The commented file is only ever in the comment-lens room; it is physically absent from writer rooms. Enforced by file placement, not instruction.
4. **Code stays byte-identical.** Only docstrings/comments are added; verify with `python3 $SKILL/verify_code.py <target.py> $RUN/FINAL_<voice>.py` — it strips docstrings from both ASTs, compares the executable structure (line numbers excluded, so added docstrings don't register), and compiles the finished file. Exit 0 + `CODE IDENTICAL` is the pass; anything else prints the offending construct. Do NOT hand-roll this with `strip.py` (it writes to a file and prints only a status line, so a stdout capture comes back empty and reads as a false mismatch).
5. **Warn about user-global memory.** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` loads under `claude -p` regardless of cwd. Tell the user it may influence the comments; it's out of scope to neutralize.
6. **Never auto-commit.** After the human approves the report, you may write the finished file onto the working tree (uncommitted, reversible) on an explicit confirm; never `git add`/`git commit`. The human reviews the diff and commits.
7. **Push back on lossy, bad-data, risky, or out-of-directive requests — do not blindly comply.** When the human asks for something that loses data (drop a fact they kept, a blunt body-drop), **adds bad data** (a fact the code contradicts, or low-value water-cooler chatter that should not become a comment even though they asked for it), is risky (apply without reading the report, anything that touches code, committing, apply-all-without-review), or falls outside what the skill does, name the consequence and offer options via `AskUserQuestion` instead of just doing it — e.g. *"that drops the by-reference fact you kept: tighten instead / drop anyway / cancel / re-roll with a new rule"*, or *"the code contradicts this" / "this reads as noise: add anyway / rephrase / cancel"*. Comply only on explicit confirmation, then trust them. The live gates where this bites: the **picker** (empty / all-dropped), **add-fact** (`stubify` status=contradicted or `concern` set), **apply-all** (skipping review), and the **refine** lossy ops.
8. **Run each blocking phase in the background and stream its progress.** Phase 1 and phase 2 each run as one `claude -p` that takes minutes and prints nothing until it finishes — never call it as a foreground `Bash` (that strands the user staring at a stalled turn). Instead, **in one turn**: (a) tell the user what is running and the rough duration (e.g. *"Phase 1: 3 code lenses + comment lens + ledger-writer + validator loop, clean room, a few minutes"*); (b) launch the phase driver with **`Bash(run_in_background: true)`**; (c) arm a **`Monitor`** (non-persistent, `timeout_ms` ~3600000 — batch/comparison runs legitimately exceed 30 min) on `python3 $SKILL/progress_watch.py <room...>`, which emits one chat event per pipeline artifact as it lands (stripped → lenses → ledger → writer passes → selector → final). **Pass EVERY active room** — a library batch runs one room per file, and a single-room watch silently misses every other file's events; a comparison run's rooms are `$RUN/v/<voice>`. For a phase-1-only watch add **`--until phase1.json`** (phase 1 never writes `FINAL_*.py`, so the default terminal never fires and the watch idles to its deadline). Progress then streams into the session with no second terminal. Proceed to the next step on the **phase task's completion notification**; if that task exits with an error before the final artifact, `TaskStop` the Monitor and surface the failure. (The same `progress_watch.py` invocation still works if the user prefers to watch from their own terminal.)

## Procedure

### Runbook (the orchestrator follows these literally; [phases.md](phases.md) explains each phase's internals)
Let `SKILL=.github/skills/regen-comments`. Allocate the run room with `RUN=$(python3 $SKILL/rooms.py new <slug>)` — a fresh, unique `mkdtemp` dir. **Never hand-build `/tmp/regen-cr/<slug>-<n>`:** two parallel runs guess the same name and land in the same room, and a leftover dir poisons the run with a prior run's stale artifacts. Each batched file (folder/library/`--all`) likewise gets its own `mkdtemp` room.
0. **Preflight (in-session):** `python3 $SKILL/preflight.py --expect-email <the account THIS session runs as>` (pass the session's account email from your context, so it can compare). It confirms `claude` is on PATH, runnable, and **logged in**, and reports the CLI's account from `claude auth status`. Every phase shells out to `claude -p`, which uses the CLI's OWN login — if that differs from your session's account (different org / model access / subscription / billing), the clean-room work silently runs under the wrong account. An **ACCOUNT MISMATCH fails preflight (exit 1)**, same as missing / not logged in: **STOP and tell the user — the run proceeds ONLY on their explicit agreement**, never on your own judgment; an unknown-account warning likewise gets surfaced for their confirmation before any phase runs. If you don't know the session's account email, run it without `--expect-email` and surface the CLI account for the user to confirm.
0b. **Resolve target, genre, scope (in-session):** turn what the user said (prose, a path, a flag, a method) into a concrete **target**, **genre** (`--kind`), and **scope**, per [Targeting, genre, and scope](#targeting-genre-and-scope). Use `python3 $SKILL/genre.py detect <path>` for path-based genre; the user's words/flags ("unit tests"/`--tests`, "functional tests"/`--functional-tests`, "examples"/`--examples`, `--all`) otherwise. **Verify a folder lane exists** (`ls` the `tests/`/`functional_tests/`/`examples/` dir) before using it, and `ls` a named library to its source dir. State the resolved target + genre + scope and confirm (a quick prose confirm, or fold it into the voice gate). `--all` → **push back on cost** (invariant 7) before running. **Method scope** → run phase 1 + phase 2 on the file, then `regen_method.py <file> $RUN <voice> <symbol>` splices only that symbol onto the original (every other symbol keeps its existing comments) and verifies; present/apply only it.
1. **Voice gate (in-session):** if `--voice <key>` given, use it; else print the in-session numbered text menu (see [The voice pick menu](#the-voice-pick-menu-when-no---voice)) — every voice from `voices.json` with its persona + first cached-preview sentence, `plain` marked default — then **stop and wait** for the user to type a number or key, and map it to the voice. NOT an `AskUserQuestion`. (Run `gen_voice_previews.py` once to populate previews; `--create-voice` → registry-add flow, then stop.)
1b. **Folder / library / `--all` scope (in-session):** build the cross-file ledger once — `LIBROOM=$(python3 $SKILL/rooms.py new <slug>-lib)`, then `python3 $SKILL/regen_phase0.py <lib_dir> $LIBROOM` → `$LIBROOM/LIBRARY_FACTS.md` (domain + cross-file contracts + glossary). Phase 0 is itself a multi-minute clean-room call — run it per invariant 8 (background + Monitor on `progress_watch.py $LIBROOM --until LIBRARY_FACTS.md`). Then run steps 2–8 **per file**, the orchestrator passing `--lib $LIBROOM/LIBRARY_FACTS.md` and `--kind <genre>` to phase 1 automatically. **To go faster**, batch the gate-free phases (concurrency 2-3 — each pipeline is its own `claude -p` fan-out, so higher oversubscribes); `regen_batch.py` mints a FRESH unique room per file (`mkdtemp`, so parallel files never collide): `python3 $SKILL/regen_batch.py phase1 3 --kind <genre> [--lib $LIBROOM/LIBRARY_FACTS.md] <files...>` (writes a room manifest), pickers per room, then `python3 $SKILL/regen_batch.py phase2 3 <voice> <rooms...>` (phase 2 reads each room's genre from its `phase1.json`). For `--all`, run this once per lane (`code` source / `test` / `functional_test` / `example`), reading each lane's manifest before the next overwrites it. A single-file or single-method target skips this step.
2. **Phase 1 (clean-room grounding):** `python3 $SKILL/regen_phase1.py <target.py> $RUN [--kind <genre>] [--without-comment-triage] [--lib <LIBRARY_FACTS.md>]` (pass `--kind` from the resolved genre — it otherwise defaults to the path's detected genre; `--lib` is supplied automatically in folder/library mode). **Launch it in the background with the progress Monitor (invariant 8).** It strips, captures the header for preservation, then runs the triage workflow as one clean-room `claude -p` — **code** genre: 3 lenses + comment lens + ledger-writer + **validator/converge loop**; **test / functional_test / example**: the genre triage (one genre-ledger pass + comment lens + a single validate, no converge loop). It prints the **questionable facts** + whether the validator flags issues, and writes `$RUN/{ledger_provisional.md, ledger.json, preserve.json, validation.json, phase1.json}` (phase1.json records the `genre`).
3. **Validator gate (in-session):** the ledger-writer already re-ran against the validator up to 4× inside phase 1. Only if `phase1.json` shows `needs_user: true` (still flagged after the loop) do you ESCALATE — present the flagged facts (`validation.json`) plus a recommendation in an `AskUserQuestion` with a free-text window, then apply the user's steer before phase 2.
4. **Picker (in-session, the one human gate):** present the **low/med-confidence** facts (`phase1.json` `questionable`) for a keep/drop; high-confidence facts (code- OR comment-derived) are auto-kept and not shown. **Present each fact by its `gloss` — the plain-English sentence — NEVER the raw `stub`.** The stub is deliberately telegraphic, writer-facing notation ("two clock timelines", "aliasing past half-period"); shown bare at the gate it reads as gibberish the human cannot judge. Option label = a short plain phrase from the gloss; option description = the full gloss + confidence + source. If a fact has no gloss (an old room), expand the stub into one plain sentence yourself before presenting — that is presentation, not code judgment. Shape the gate to the count so the tool never errors: **0** → skip it (say everything was high-confidence and auto-kept); **1** → single-select **Keep / Drop** (a 1-option multi-select is invalid); **2–4** → multi-select `AskUserQuestion`, one option per fact, checked = keep; **5+** → an in-session numbered text list, user types the numbers to **drop** (empty = keep all). Write `$RUN/ledger_final.md` = `ledger_provisional.md` minus the **rejected** lines (the .md carries stubs only — glosses live in `ledger.json` and never reach the writers). **Push back (invariant 7)** on an empty/all-dropped answer — re-confirm before dropping a batch rather than silently discarding it.
5. **Phase 2 (clean-room write):** `python3 $SKILL/regen_phase2.py $RUN <voice>` (it reads the genre from `$RUN/phase1.json`; `--kind <genre>` overrides). **Launch it in the background with the progress Monitor (invariant 8).** Runs the writer workflow **in the genre's shape** (4 passes + a best-of-4 selector + an independent summarizer; `code` = behavior + caller contract, `test`/`functional_test` = one-sentence claim docstrings, `example` = dense near-line annotation), copies the chosen pass to `merged.py`, reattaches the preserve lane, writes `$RUN/{FINAL_<voice>.py, merged.py, pick.json, summary.json}`. **Then verify the code is untouched (invariant 4):** `python3 $SKILL/verify_code.py <target.py> $RUN/FINAL_<voice>.py` — require exit 0 / `CODE IDENTICAL` before presenting anything; if it reports CHANGED or a compile error, stop and surface it instead of rendering the report.
5b. **Comparison run (2–3 voices) — replaces steps 5–7:** `python3 $SKILL/regen_phase2_multi.py $RUN <voice1> <voice2> [voice3]` generates each voice in its OWN room `$RUN/v/<voice>/` (a full run room — the shared phase-1 inputs are copied in and `regen_phase2.py` runs there, so each voice gets its own `FINAL_<voice>.py`, `runs/`, `pick.json`, `legibility.json`, isolated from the others). **Launch in the background with the progress Monitor (invariant 8).** **Verify each (invariant 4):** `python3 $SKILL/verify_code.py <target.py> $RUN/v/<voice>/FINAL_<voice>.py` for every voice. Then `python3 $SKILL/render_compare.py $RUN <target.py> <voice1> <voice2> [voice3]` → `$RUN/compare.html` (per-symbol docstrings side by side + each voice's selection rationale + legibility flags; auto-opens). Surface it (`SendUserFile` + the `file://` line) and tell the human to read it. Each voice card carries a **pick radio + notes box**; the page's **Copy selection** button yields a `regen-comments voice (<file>): <key>` blob the human pastes back (typing the voice name in chat works too, and a served page's **Submit to session** button delivers the same blob as a Monitor event — serve with `serve_report.py $RUN compare.html`). On the pick, run steps 6–7 **in that voice's room** `$RUN/v/<voice>/` — `flag_legibility.py`, then `render_report.py` there, which gives the per-symbol picker over that voice's 4 cached passes — and continue to step 8 in that room (a complete run room, so the Step 8 tools work unchanged). **Apply** copies the **chosen** voice's `$RUN/v/<voice>/FINAL_<voice>.py` onto the target.
   **Library scope + multiple voices = a voice ELECTION on a sample file, not a per-file vote.** Do not generate every voice for every file — N files × 3 voices doubles-to-triples the run for no added signal once the register is chosen. Run the multi-voice comparison on the FIRST file only; the human's compare.html pick (or typed voice) elects the run's voice **globally**; the remaining files then run normal single-voice phase 2 in the winner (`regen_batch.py phase2 <conc> <winner> <rooms...>`). A per-file override stays available on request — re-run that one room's phase 2 with a different voice (`regen_phase2.py <room> <other-voice>`) — but the default is every file switches to the elected voice. State the cost difference up front when confirming a library comparison (election ≈ one comparison + N−1 single runs, vs N comparisons).
6. **Legibility flag (in-session):** `python3 $SKILL/flag_legibility.py $RUN <voice>` → `$RUN/legibility.json` (a clean-room pass that flags any docstring/comment **sentence that reads awkwardly**, flag-only, never rewrites). A convoluted sentence is a rare stochastic roll the writer occasionally produces and nothing else in the pipeline watches for it; this is the watcher. Conservative — an empty list is the normal, good result. The flags surface in the report; the human fixes them in the refine loop (Step 8). A second, **deterministic** pass — `flag_tics.py` (run automatically inside phase 2, no LLM) — writes `$RUN/tics.json` flagging **AI discourse-marker tics** ("that's the whole X", "here's the thing", "the one thing", "this is the X that") and **voice-descriptor leaks** (a distinctive phrase from the active voice's persona that landed in a comment but is NOT in the code, e.g. cutler's "3 a.m."). Both surface next to the legibility flags in the report; both are flag-only, cut in the refine loop. Upstream of both, phase 2 already auto-routed any flagged symbol to a clean cached pass where one existed (`autoroute_tics.py`, recorded as `autoroute` in `pick.json`) and spent ONE `polish.py` round on the rest; violations that survive land in `$RUN/bans.json` and flag in the report — the human clears that tail via pick-a-different-take or edit-it-myself, never more LLM rounds.
7. **Report (in-session):** `python3 $SKILL/render_report.py $RUN <voice> <target.py>` → `$RUN/spec.json` + `$RUN/picker.html` on the shared picker (it auto-opens unless `REGEN_NO_OPEN=1`; flags surface in an open page-top section and as ⚠ warnings on their cards; every card renders open). **Folder / library scope:** render ONE faceted page instead — `python3 $SKILL/render_library.py <outdir> <voice> <room>=<original> ...` (pairs from `batch_manifest.json`) → `<outdir>/spec.json` + `picker.html`: card ids namespaced `<file.py>#<sym>`, a select-style file facet plus flagged/clean chips, per-file context sections, ONE combined blob covering every touched file. The page is **interactive**: each card shows the original docstring above the candidates side by side — the selector's winner leftmost and pre-checked as **suggested**, every *differing* cached writer pass beside it (docstring + comparison chips + a full-symbol expander showing inline comments; click a box to pick it; 4+ scroll horizontally) — and an **edit** box below, seeded with the suggested docstring: adjust it in place and its exact text rides back on its own `edit` blob line (newlines survive; the note box stays a plain note). The symbol's ledger facts sit behind a detail fold; a sticky bar serializes picks + edits + notes into the paste-back blob. Also surface it with `SendUserFile`, print its `file://` line, and **explicitly tell the human to open/read the page before deciding** — do not assume they have seen it. If any sentences were flagged, name them so the human knows what to look at. **Serve + submit loop (recommended):** launch `PICKER_NO_OPEN=1 python3 $SKILL/../_shared/picker/serve_picker.py $RUN` (library scope: `<outdir>`) with `Bash(run_in_background)`, `open` the URL from its `SERVING` line (the session is the only opener), and arm a `Monitor` on its stdout — it prints one `SELECTION RECEIVED -> <path>` line per submit, delivering the blob mid-gate with no paste, and a browser refresh re-renders the page whenever `spec.json` changed. Set `REGEN_NO_OPEN=1` on refine-loop re-renders so they don't also open a stale `file://` copy (the human refreshes the served tab instead). Without the server, the `file://` page hides Submit and the Copy-selection paste-back works unchanged. `TaskStop` the server when the loop exits on Apply or Discard.
8. **Refine + apply loop (in-session) — KEEP LOOPING until the human Applies or Discards:** present an `AskUserQuestion` "What next?" each round (**re-run `flag_legibility.py` + `flag_tics.py` then re-render the report first**, so any flagged sentences, tics, or leaks a refine introduced or fixed are current). Because `AskUserQuestion` allows ≤4 options, the loop is two nested questions:
   - **Round menu (≤4 opts):** **Refine a symbol** · **Apply to the repo** · **Discard (no changes)** (in library mode also **Apply all remaining**). A *refine* never exits the loop; only Apply/Discard do.
   - **Selection blob (an alternative to the Refine branch):** if the human pastes the page's `PICKS — regen-comments apply (…)` blob (or a legacy `regen-comments apply (<file>): …` one, or types deviations like `get=run-3`), save it to `$RUN/selection.txt`; a `SELECTION RECEIVED` Monitor event from `serve_picker.py` means the blob is already there — same channel, same gates from here. Run `python3 $SKILL/apply_selection.py parse $RUN/selection.txt` and **read the picks, edits, and notes first — invariant 7 applies here** (an `edit` that drops a kept ledger fact or states something the code contradicts gets a push-back before anything is written). Then `python3 $SKILL/apply_selection.py apply $RUN <voice> $RUN/selection.txt` — it splices each `run-N` pick from the cached passes (splice guard: code identity) and replaces each `edit` symbol's docstring with the human's exact text. **A library blob carries one section per file:** apply it once per room with the basename filter — `apply <room> <voice> <blob> <file.py>` (the room from `batch_manifest.json`; the applier refuses a multi-file blob without the filter). Then re-run `polish.py` (the cached passes are pre-polish; no-op when clean), `verify_code.py`, both flaggers, and `render_report.py`, and **return to the round menu** — a blob is a batch refine, not an exit.
   - **If Refine →** ask *which symbol* (offer up to 3 + free-text "Other"), then ask *the change* (4 opts): **roll the dice** · **tighten** · **edit the facts** · **write it myself**. Run the matching tool, re-render (it re-opens), then return to the round menu.
       - roll the dice: `splice_symbol.py $RUN/FINAL_<voice>.py $RUN/runs/run-<N>.py <symbol> $RUN/FINAL_<voice>.py` cycling N=1..4; once exhausted, `regen_symbol.py $RUN <voice> <symbol>` for a fresh take.
       - tighten (shorter, fact-preserving): `tighten_symbol.py $RUN <voice> <symbol>`. It keeps the summary + Args/Returns/Raises + every ledger fact and cuts only wordy body prose, then prints a KEPT/DROPPED report. If it reports DROPPED facts, **push back** (invariant 7) before continuing.
       - edit the facts: sub-ask *drop / edit / add?*. Drop or edit → change that fact's line in `$RUN/ledger_final.md`, then `regen_symbol.py $RUN <voice> <symbol>`. Add → ask *correction or your-own-note?*: correction → `stubify_fact.py $RUN "<fact>"`, act on the verdict (confirmed + no concern → append stub + `regen_symbol.py`; **contradicted OR `concern` set (clearly-wrong / low-value noise) → push back per invariant 7**, comply on confirm; unverifiable+needs_source → ask for a URL/desc; else trust); your-own-note → ask initials, add `# NOTE(<initials>): <verbatim>` at the symbol (offer voiced vs verbatim) — **push back first if the note reads as useless**.
       - write it myself: replace that symbol's docstring with the human's exact text (in-session `Edit`; then `tics.py` + AST check).
       - **A raw "drop the body / delete this" request is lossy — do NOT just do it.** Offer **tighten** (keeps the facts) vs drop-anyway vs cancel (invariant 7). After any ledger edit: `drift_check.py $RUN <voice> <symbol> "<what changed>"`; if it flags sure-stale symbols, offer to regen those too (never block).
   - **If Apply →** `cp $RUN/FINAL_<voice>.py <target.py>` (working tree, uncommitted, reversible); tell the human to review the diff in their editor; exit the loop. **Never `git add`/`git commit`.** (Library mode: advance to the next file's report+loop. **Apply all remaining** writes every remaining file unreviewed — **push back (invariant 7)**: confirm the human accepts skipping the per-file review before doing it.)
   - **If Discard →** exit the loop, write nothing.

## Done when
A finished commented file exists for the chosen voice, with: executable code byte-identical to the original, the correctness-critical facts correct against the code and stated explicitly, the load-bearing facts present (the caller's contract in docstrings, line-level gotchas as inline comments), preserve lane reattached verbatim, zero mechanical-ban violations, reads cleanly (in voice when one was chosen) with any awkward sentence flagged by the legibility watcher — surfaced via the decision page `picker.html` (independent summary + ledger + before/after + rationale + legibility flags, auto-opened or served) the human was pointed at, refined as they chose through the Step 8 loop, and the loop exited on their explicit Apply (written to the working tree, uncommitted) or Discard, with nothing committed automatically.

## Creating a voice (`--create-voice`)
A separate mode that adds a voice to the shared registry plus its real-text sample; it does not regenerate any file's comments. The registry serves every voice-consuming skill, so a voice added here is immediately available to them all. The orchestrator runs it interactively:
1. **Name** — ask the human for a person (or a clear disposition), e.g. "Grace Hopper".
2. **Draft** — `python3 $SKILL/create_voice.py gen "<name>"` drafts a one-sentence descriptive persona in the registry's house style (clean-room `claude -p`) — or the human pastes a draft from any tool they prefer; `add` validates form, not authorship.
3. **Edit** — show the draft; let the human edit it via `AskUserQuestion` (free-text) until they are happy.
4. **Sample** — source 1–3 short excerpts of the person's real prose and write `$SKILL/../_shared/voices/voice_samples/<key>.md`: their natural domain, the era whose register matches the persona, attribution in the header bullets only, prose only under `## Excerpt` headings — full sourcing rules and proven fetch routes in [voice_samples/README.md](../_shared/voices/voice_samples/README.md). The hunt is in-session orchestrator work (WebSearch / WebFetch + judgment); verify `python3 $SKILL/../_shared/voices/voice_sample.py <key>` prints prose only. If the human declines a sample, the voice runs persona-only.
5. **Test** — run the normal pipeline on a target the human supplies, render the decision page, and **do not write back**. Optionally enter the Step 8 refine loop. Testing on a fresh user-supplied target (not a baked fixture) keeps the test from going stale.
6. **Save** — on accept, `python3 $SKILL/create_voice.py add <key> "<final persona>"` appends the persona, checks the sample file, and generates its pick-menu preview (`gen_voice_previews.py`, sample-aware). The voice is then usable as `--voice <key>` and appears with a preview.
- **Success:** the new persona is in `voices.json` with a cached preview and (normally) a `voice_samples/<key>.md` whose loader output is prose-only; validated by the human on a real target; the committed registry stays clean if they decline.

## Reference files
- [phases.md](phases.md) — what each phase does inside its clean room (lenses, validator, writer spine, selector, auto-route, polish, reattach, flaggers, report), with per-step success criteria. Read it when a phase misbehaves, when changing the pipeline, or when an artifact needs explaining beyond what the Runbook states.
- [tools.md](tools.md) — every bundled script's contract (what it does, inputs, outputs, sharp edges). The Runbook names each tool at its call site with the exact invocation; read tools.md before calling one outside its Runbook slot.
- [TESTPLAN.md](TESTPLAN.md) — mechanical checks, read-only clean-room validations per genre/scope, trigger-routing evals, and the cold-session script for the human gates.

## Patterns to avoid
- Running any code-reading agent via the in-session Workflow tool (poison risk + no file isolation) — always `claude -p` from `/tmp`.
- Putting the human picker inside a `claude -p` (it can't ask) — the gate is in-session, between phases.
- Letting the selector **rewrite or merge** across passes — it only picks one whole pass by number, and phase 2 copies that file verbatim; a rewrite is unvalidated new text and a fresh failure surface (it once shipped a reworded inversion). Per-symbol consolidation exists only as the **human's** decision page (`picker.html`): every candidate is verbatim text from a complete pass, the human reads what they pick, `splice_symbol`'s guard keeps the code identical, and the assembled file goes back through polish + verify + the flaggers (no watcher saw that combination whole). An *agent* merging or rewording across passes stays banned.
- Writing correctness-critical ledger facts as fluent sentences (writers echo them verbatim, collapsing voice) — telegraphic fragments only.
- `git checkout CLAUDE.md` to "restore" it — may re-enable an `@AGENTS.md` include the user disabled.
